1.meaning: Alif-Lam-Mim: three Arabic letters recited individually as separate letter-names. They belong to the 'disconnected letters' (al-huruf al-muqattaʿa) that open certain chapters of the Qur'an. They are not a word with lexical meaning; their precise significance is regarded as known to Allah, though they draw attention to the inimitability of the revelation, which is composed from these very letters of the Arabic alphabet.
1.grammar: These are letter-names spelled out and recited one by one, not an inflected word, so they carry no case ending, tense, person, or number. They function as a self-standing opening and take no grammatical role within a sentence.

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: "signs / verses / tokens" — the plural of āya, a 'sign' or evident token that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a verse of revelation, each one a sign.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -u is the nominative case, the form taken as the subject of a sentence or the leading term of a possessive chain ('the signs OF …').
2.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, token, mark

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: 'The Wise.' An adjective describing one possessing ḥikma — sound, perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right and fitting place. As a divine attribute it denotes flawless wisdom in all decree and command.

parts.en: wise / full of wisdom (in the genitive, '-i')

4.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('deeply/perfectly wise'). The al- means 'the.' The final -i vowel is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition, or when describing a noun that is itself genitive, or linking in an 'of …' relationship.
4.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to be wise, judge soundly, put things in their right place

1.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

1.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

2.meaning: 'Mercy' — compassion and loving kindness shown by bestowing good and relieving hardship. From the same root as 'womb,' it carries a sense of nurturing tenderness.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), an integral letter of the word. The tanwīn fatḥ on that ة (-tan) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case of a direct object or of something granted. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the shadda written on وَّ reflects a recitation convention (idghām at the junction with the preceding word), not an assimilation of the conjunction itself.
2.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tender care

3.meaning: for the good-doers
3.grammar: prepositional phrase: preposition لِ + definite article + noun, sound masculine plural in genitive case (مُحْسِنِينَ Form IV active participle of أَحْسَنَ)
3.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, to do good

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: "They establish / set up / keep up," from a verb meaning to make something stand firm and upright — used for performing and maintaining something properly and steadfastly (as with prayer).
2.grammar: The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense, with the full "-ūna" ending showing the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement). The verb is the causative (Form IV) pattern: "to make stand / cause to be upright," hence "to establish."
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; causatively, to set up or establish

3.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
3.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

4.meaning: "And they give / they bring," from a verb meaning to hand over, bestow, or bring something to someone — to render what is due, such as giving alms.
4.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense, with the full "-ūna" ending signaling the indicative mood. The verb is the causative (Form IV) pattern, conveying "to cause to come / to give over."
4.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; causatively, to bring or give

5.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
5.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
5.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

6.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

7.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
7.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

8.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

9.meaning: To have firm, certain knowledge or conviction — to be sure of something with no doubt, especially regarding unseen realities. It is stronger than ordinary 'believing': it conveys settled certainty.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form IV) in the third person masculine plural: 'they have certainty / firmly believe'. The imperfect prefix is yu- (يُ); the stem root-pattern begins with wāw (from أَوْقَنَ → يُوقِنُ), so the prefix and stem together are pronounced yū-. The -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) in the indicative mood (denoting an ongoing or habitual action).

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

3.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

6.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
6.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

7.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

8.meaning: 'The successful / the ones who flourish' — those who attain what they seek and are saved from what they fear. The underlying sense is of prospering, thriving, and winning through to lasting wellbeing and salvation, not merely worldly success.
8.grammar: A definite active participle (Form IV) in the masculine plural: 'the ones who succeed/prosper'. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate identifying who someone is.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

2.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
2.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
2.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: purchases / buys
4.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form VIII (اشترى), 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood
4.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, to sell, to exchange

5.meaning: idle tales / vain amusement
5.grammar: noun, masculine singular in accusative case (direct object), Form I verbal noun of لَهَا
5.root: ل-ه-و (l-h-w) — to be distracted, amuse oneself idly

6.meaning: The speech/account/narration — a piece of talk, a report, story, or statement; that which is related or told. With 'the', it points to a particular discourse or account.
6.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… OF …'). The pattern faʿīl gives a thing-told sense: an account or narration.
6.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen anew; to relate, narrate, recount

7.meaning: So that He should let go astray / to lead astray — for the purpose of causing someone to lose the way. The leading 'so that' particle sets up purpose; the verb is the causative 'make/let go astray'.
7.grammar: The purpose particle li- ('so that') + a present-tense Form IV (causative) verb in the 'he' form; the yu- prefix is the causative pattern's marker, 'to make/cause to…'. The -a ending is the subjunctive, regularly triggered by li- of purpose — 'so that he may lead astray'.
7.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

8.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

9.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
9.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
11.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
11.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

12.meaning: knowledge
12.grammar: noun, masculine singular, genitive case with tanwīn (indefinite), functioning as object of preposition بِ implied

13.meaning: and takes it (as mockery)

parts.en: it / them (3rd person feminine singular pronoun suffix)

13.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form VIII (اتَّخَذَ), 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (لِ before it implied); with attached object pronoun هَا

14.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
14.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
14.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
15.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

16.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

17.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

18.meaning: 'Humiliating / disgracing / degrading' — an active participle describing something that brings abasement and disgrace upon its object.
18.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word, like '-ing' in English) from the causative (form IV) pattern, meaning 'one that causes humiliation.' The -un ending (indefinite nominative tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun in the nominative case — the case of a subject or, commonly, of something described as existing ('a humiliating [thing]').
18.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — being lowly, easy, contemptible; hence humiliation

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: and turns away
5.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form II (وَلَّى), 3rd person masculine singular, meaning to turn away / turn one's back
5.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to turn toward/away

6.meaning: arrogantly / disdainfully
6.grammar: active participle, Form X (اسْتَكْبَرَ), masculine singular, accusative case with tanwīn, functioning as ḥāl (circumstantial descriptor)
6.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, to be arrogant

7.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
7.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

8.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
8.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

9.meaning: he hears them

parts.en: them / it (3rd person feminine singular pronoun suffix)

9.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; with object pronoun هَا (referring to آيات — the verses)

10.meaning: as if / as though

parts.en: as if / as though (particle of comparison)

10.grammar: particle: كَ (like) + أَنَّ (that/indeed), used to introduce a simile in which the following noun is in accusative

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: his two ears
12.grammar: noun, dual form of أُذُن (ear), genitive case (يْهِ suffix = dual genitive + 3rd person masculine possessive pronoun), object of كَأَنَّ (in accusative function assimilated to genitive by suffix)

13.meaning: "Heaviness, a weight; deafness." Literally a heavy load or burden; used of the ears it means a heaviness that blocks hearing — i.e., deafness or hardness of hearing.
13.grammar: A singular noun, indefinite ("a heaviness"). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness together with the accusative case — the case a noun takes as the object of a verb or when otherwise governed into it.
13.root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r) — to be heavy, weighty; gravity, dignity

14.meaning: So give him glad tidings / announce good news to him: to convey welcome, joyful news that visibly gladdens. The command is directed at one male addressee and carries an attached 'him' as the one receiving the good news.
14.grammar: A Form II imperative (command) addressed to a second-person masculine singular ('you, give good news'), with attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The prefix fa- means 'so/then'. The intensive Form II conveys actively delivering joyful news. A command form takes no case vowel; its base ends in a silent stop (sukūn) before the pronoun.
14.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; to gladden

15.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
15.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

16.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
16.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: Gardens — lush, densely shaded enclosures whose foliage covers the ground; the plural of the word for a garden, used pre-eminently for the Gardens of Paradise.
7.grammar: A feminine sound plural of 'janna' (garden), formed with the '-āt' plural ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… are gardens').
7.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; lush garden whose growth covers the earth

8.meaning: Bliss, delight, abundant ease — a state of luxuriant comfort and joyful well-being; the lasting felicity associated with Paradise.
8.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' is pronounced as the following 'n,' giving 'an-naʿīm'). A noun meaning 'bliss/delight.' The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case — used after a preposition or to link a noun to a preceding one ('… OF bliss').

1.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
1.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
3.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
3.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
5.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
5.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

6.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
6.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

7.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
7.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

8.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
8.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
8.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
1.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

2.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
2.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

3.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
3.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
3.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

4.meaning: Supports, props, or pillars — the columns or poles upon which something rests or is held up.
4.grammar: A noun (collective/plural in sense) carrying the -in ending, which is genitive together with indefiniteness ('nunation'). This -in typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun, conveying 'of pillars / any pillars'.
4.root: ع-م-د (ʿ-m-d) — to support, prop up, set on a pillar

5.meaning: You (plural) see it / are seeing it — to perceive something with the eyes, with the thing seen referred to as 'it' (feminine).
5.grammar: A present-tense verb: the ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -na ending marks the plural, so together 'you all see'. The attached -hā is the object pronoun 'it/her', referring to something grammatically feminine.
5.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold

6.meaning: 'And He cast / threw down' — to fling, place, or set down firmly. The Form IV verb conveys casting something into position, as firm masses set upon the earth.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form IV (to cast, throw down). The bare form ending in the long -ā (a weak/defective root) marks a completed action by a single masculine 'he' ('and he cast').

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: Firmly anchored, towering mountains — heights that stand immovable and steady, often pictured as stabilising the earth.
9.grammar: A plural noun in the 'broken plural' pattern, denoting mountains as firmly fixed. The final -a here is the accusative ending typical of this diptote pattern (which resists the usual -in), marking the word as an object or in a similar role.
9.root: ر-س-و (r-s-w) — to be firm, anchored, immovably fixed

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: To sway, lurch, or shake from side to side; to be unsteady and tip about, as ground that quakes beneath one's feet.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (hollow root, the middle weak letter showing as long -ī). The ta- prefix marks a single feminine 'it/she' as the doer; the final -a is the subjunctive, the mood used after particles of purpose or negation ('that it sway').

12.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
12.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

13.meaning: And He scattered, spread, or dispersed abroad; to send creatures or things out in all directions.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb joined by 'wa' ('and'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he scattered'); the bare ending with no added suffix is the default form for a completed action done by 'he'.

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
16.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'a moving/walking creature / a beast / any living thing that treads the earth' — broadly, any animal that moves along the ground.
17.grammar: A singular indefinite feminine noun (originally an active participle, 'one that moves/treads'). The ending -tin combines the feminine marker (tā' marbūṭa) with tanwīn showing indefiniteness and the genitive case — the form typically used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …'). The final '-n' sound is spoken but unwritten.
17.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep/walk gently along the ground

18.meaning: 'And we sent down' — to cause something to descend or come down from a higher place, often used of sending down rain, sustenance, or revelation. Prefixed with 'and' and marked for a 'we' subject in the past.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (meaning 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks 'we' as the doer, giving 'we sent down'. The wa- prefix is 'and'. The causative form distinguishes it from simply 'descending' — it means causing descent.

19.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
19.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

20.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
20.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

21.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
21.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

22.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form IV (أَنْبَتَ), 1st person plural (royal/majestic we), referring to Allah causing plants to grow

23.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
23.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
25.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

26.meaning: A noun meaning 'a spouse / mate / one of a pair' — a husband or a wife; more broadly, one member of a matched pair.

parts.en: spouse / mate / member of a pair (stem)

26.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending ('a spouse'), the case used after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of a spouse').

27.meaning: Noble, generous, honorable: marked by high worth, dignity, and openhanded generosity. Applied to things it means excellent and valuable; applied to giving it means abundant and gracious.
27.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, indefinite. The -in (tanwīn) ending marks the indefinite genitive: it agrees with and describes a preceding indefinite genitive noun ('a … and noble …'), or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: (the) creation (of)
2.grammar: noun, masculine singular, nominative case in iḍāfa (construct) with following genitive; Form I verbal noun of خَلَقَ
2.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: so show me
4.grammar: verb, imperative, Form IV (أَرَى), 2nd person masculine plural; with 1st person singular object pronoun نِي

5.meaning: What? — an interrogative asking about a thing; often a compound of the question word 'what' with the demonstrative 'that'.
5.grammar: A compound question word, 'mā' ('what') joined to 'dhā' ('that / which'), used to ask 'what is it that…?'. It is indeclinable and does not change its ending.
5.root: — (no triliteral root; interrogative)

6.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
6.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

9.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

10.meaning: Rather / nay, but — a particle that cancels or corrects what came before and introduces a contrasting truth: 'no — instead …'. It sets aside a prior idea and replaces it.
10.grammar: A particle of retraction and correction; it does not change endings on other words. Its base form is 'bal'; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a cluster.

11.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
11.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
13.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

14.meaning: Making clear, manifest, or plain; that which clarifies and is itself evident. Used of something that both shows itself plainly and makes other things distinct and unambiguous.
14.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective, meaning 'clarifying / clear'. The 'mu-' prefix marks the doer of the action. The final '-in' marks it indefinite ('a …') and genitive, the case used after prepositions or as the second term of a possessive.

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

3.meaning: Luqman (proper name, accusative)
3.grammar: proper noun, diptote (ممنوع من الصرف), accusative/genitive case (no tanwīn), name of the wise man mentioned in Quran

4.meaning: Wisdom — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; knowledge joined to right action. The root conveys restraint and setting things firmly in order, as a wise ruling brings matters under proper control.
4.grammar: Definite noun (with 'the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. given or attained).
4.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern, restrain; wisdom

5.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
5.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

6.meaning: be grateful / give thanks
6.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form I (شَكَرَ), 2nd person masculine singular
6.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to be grateful, to thank

7.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
8.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

9.meaning: is grateful / gives thanks
9.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; used in conditional clause
9.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to be grateful, to thank

10.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
10.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

11.meaning: he is grateful / gives thanks
11.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood (مرفوع)
11.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to be grateful, to thank

12.meaning: For / to himself / for his own soul — nafs means the self, soul, or person (the inner self that is held to account). The li- means 'for/to,' and the attached -hi makes it 'his.'
12.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). After the preposition the noun is in the genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the -hi suffix.
12.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, the inner being

13.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
13.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

14.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
14.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

15.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
15.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: Rich, wealthy, self-sufficient; one who is free of need and dependent on no one — when said of Allah, the One utterly without need of anything.
17.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, denoting a firmly established quality of being rich and free of need. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the indefinite nominative — the case of a subject or a describing word.
17.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

18.meaning: Praiseworthy — one who is worthy of all praise, deserving and receiving commendation. As an intensive form it means richly, perpetually praiseworthy; a divine attribute of Allah.
18.grammar: A singular intensive adjective (the 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a deep, constant quality). The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or a predicate describing the subject.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

3.meaning: Luqman (proper name, nominative)
3.grammar: proper noun, diptote (ممنوع من الصرف), nominative case (subject of sentence), no tanwīn

4.meaning: to his son

parts.en: his (3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix)

4.grammar: prepositional phrase: preposition لِ + noun ابن (son) in genitive construct + 3rd person masculine possessive pronoun

5.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

6.meaning: instructing him / admonishing him

parts.en: him (3rd person masculine singular object pronoun)

6.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I (وَعَظَ), 3rd person masculine singular, indicative; with 3rd person masculine object pronoun هُ
6.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — to admonish, to counsel, to preach

7.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my little son / O my dear son' — a tender, diminutive form of address from a parent to a son, with 'my' attached.
7.grammar: A vocative with the particle 'yā' for addressing someone. The base is an affectionate diminutive of 'son'. The attached possessive is the first-person -ī ('my'); because the diminutive stem already ends in a doubled yāʾ, the possessive -ī merges with it and the word is pronounced 'bunayya'. The whole is a loving 'O my dear son'.
7.root: ب-ن-ي / ب-ن-و (b-n-y) — son, offspring, to build

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: associate partners (with Allah)
9.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form IV (أَشْرَكَ), 2nd person masculine singular, used after negative lā (لَا)
9.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate, to be a partner, to commit shirk

10.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
10.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: the association of partners (shirk)
12.grammar: noun, masculine singular, definite (with article), accusative case; Form I verbal noun (مصدر) referring to polytheism / shirk
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate, to share, to commit polytheism

13.meaning: is surely a great wrong / injustice
13.grammar: emphatic lām (لَ) + noun ظُلْم, masculine singular, nominative case with tanwīn, predicate of إِنَّ clause
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, to oppress, to be unjust

14.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: and We have enjoined / charged

parts.en: We enjoined / charged (past tense, Form II)

1.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form II (وَصَّى), 1st person plural (royal we), meaning to command, to enjoin, to instruct
1.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to bequeath, to enjoin, to charge with

2.meaning: the human being / man
2.grammar: noun, masculine singular, definite (with article), accusative case (direct object of وَصَّيْنَا)
2.root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be familiar; human being

3.meaning: A combination meaning roughly 'with/toward his two parents (father and mother together)'. The dual noun wālidān refers specifically to the two who gave one birth — one's father and mother as a pair — and the attached pronoun makes them 'his'.
3.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with, to, toward'). The stem is a dual noun (referring to exactly two — a father and mother together); its dual ending appears as -ay rather than -ān because it stands in the genitive/accusative form, which is also what the preposition bi- requires. The final -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his' (the -i vowel is the form this pronoun takes after an -i sound).
3.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

4.meaning: carried him / bore him

parts.en: him (3rd person masculine singular object pronoun)

4.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form I (حَمَلَ), 3rd person feminine singular (تْ suffix); with 3rd person masculine object pronoun هُ
4.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, to bear, to be pregnant

5.meaning: his mother

parts.en: his (3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix)

5.grammar: noun, feminine singular, nominative case in construct (iḍāfa) with 3rd person possessive pronoun هُ (subject of حَمَلَتْ)
5.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — mother; source, origin

6.meaning: in weakness upon weakness
6.grammar: noun, masculine singular, accusative case with tanwīn, functioning as ḥāl (circumstantial description) or mafʿūl muṭlaq
6.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, to weaken

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

8.meaning: upon weakness
8.grammar: noun, masculine singular, genitive case with tanwīn, object of preposition عَلَى (upon) in the phrase وَهْنًا عَلَى وَهْنٍ
8.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, to weaken

9.meaning: and his weaning

parts.en: his (3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix)

9.grammar: noun, masculine singular, nominative case in iḍāfa (construct) with possessive pronoun; Form III verbal noun of فَاصَلَ or Form I فِصَال meaning weaning/separation

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: two years
11.grammar: noun, dual form of عَام (year), genitive case (يْنِ suffix for dual genitive), indicating the period of nursing

12.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
12.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

13.meaning: be grateful / give thanks
13.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form I (شَكَرَ), 2nd person masculine singular
13.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to be grateful, to thank

14.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
14.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

15.meaning: and to your parents
15.grammar: prepositional phrase: conjunction وَ + preposition لِ + dual noun وَالِدَان (parents) in genitive construct + 2nd person singular possessive suffix كَ
15.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, to beget; parent

16.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

17.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
17.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
17.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: they both strive hard against you

parts.en: they both strove / pressed you hard (past tense, dual)

2.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form III (جَاهَدَ), 3rd person masculine dual (ا suffix); with 2nd person singular object pronoun كَ
2.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to strive, to exert effort

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
3.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: you associate partners (with Me)
5.grammar: verb, imperfect subjunctive (منصوب), Form IV (أَشْرَكَ), 2nd person masculine singular, after أَن (that) introducing purpose/result clause
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate, to commit shirk

6.meaning: 'In me / with me.' A preposition fused with the first-person singular pronoun, expressing attachment, belief, or trust directed toward the speaker ('me').
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī here is the first-person singular object that always follows a preposition or noun; it does not change for case. Combined sense: 'in me' or 'with me.'

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
8.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

9.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
9.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
11.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: obey both of them
13.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form IV (أَطَاعَ), 2nd person masculine singular, used after negative lā; with dual 3rd person object pronoun هُمَا (referring to both parents)

14.meaning: but accompany them both
14.grammar: verb, imperative, Form III (صَاحَبَ), 2nd person masculine singular; with dual 3rd person object pronoun هُمَا
14.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — to accompany, to be a companion

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
16.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
16.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

parts.en: kindness / what is known as right (accusative, indefinite)

17.grammar: noun/adjective, Form I passive participle used as noun, masculine singular, accusative case with tanwīn; meaning what is recognized as good/right
17.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, to recognize; what is known as good

18.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form VIII (اتَّبَعَ), 2nd person masculine singular

19.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
19.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

20.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
20.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

21.meaning: He turned back (in repentance), returned, and turned to attentively. The verb expresses turning oneself back toward something — characteristically a contrite turning to one's Lord again and again.
21.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, of the form-IV 'afʿala' pattern (from a hollow root, with the middle weak letter surfacing as the long 'ā'). The final '-a' marks completed action by 'he' ('he turned back'). The pattern conveys deliberately directing oneself back toward something.
21.root: ن-و-ب (n-w-b) — returning, turning back repeatedly, recourse

22.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

23.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
23.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

24.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
24.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

25.meaning: 'Your return / your place of returning.' A noun naming either the act of returning or the destination to which one comes back, with an attached 'your' addressed to a group: 'your (pl.) return.'

parts.en: return / place or time of returning

25.grammar: A noun of place/time (a 'where/when' noun) built from the verb 'to return.' Its -u ending is the nominative case, used for a subject or predicate. The attached -kum means 'your,' addressed to a group of people.
25.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, come back

parts.en: you (2nd person masculine plural object pronoun)

26.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form II (نَبَّأَ), 1st person singular, indicative; with 2nd person plural object pronoun كُمْ
26.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — to inform, to give news
