27.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
27.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

28.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
28.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
28.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

29.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
29.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my little son / O my dear son' — a tender, diminutive form of address from a parent to a son, with 'my' attached.
1.grammar: A vocative with the particle 'yā' for addressing someone. The base is an affectionate diminutive of 'son'. The attached possessive is the first-person -ī ('my'); because the diminutive stem already ends in a doubled yāʾ, the possessive -ī merges with it and the word is pronounced 'bunayya'. The whole is a loving 'O my dear son'.
1.root: ب-ن-ي / ب-ن-و (b-n-y) — son, offspring, to build

2.meaning: 'Indeed it (is)…' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with an attached feminine pronoun 'it/she'. inna firmly asserts and stresses the statement that follows.
2.grammar: An emphasis particle (inna) plus an attached pronoun, third person feminine singular (-hā). inna introduces and strengthens a nominal statement, and the suffixed -hā is its 'ism' (the noun governed by inna), which inna places in the accusative case. So although -hā corresponds to the English subject ('indeed it/she …'), grammatically it is the accusative ism of inna, not a nominative subject.

3.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
3.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

4.meaning: It/she is or comes to be — a verb of being expressing existence or a state, in a shortened form of the verb 'to be.'
4.grammar: A present-tense verb of being in the shortened (jussive) mood. The 'ta-' prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or 'it') subject. The jussive drops the final vowel — and here even the final 'n' of 'takun' falls away — giving the clipped sense 'is/was (not),' a form occurring after particles of negation or condition.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: The weight or measure of something — the amount that balances against it on a scale; figuratively even the tiniest equivalent quantity.
5.grammar: A noun denoting a unit of weight: 'the weight of.' The final '-a' marks the accusative case, here typical of a noun functioning as the object of a verb. It also stands as the first term of a possessive pairing ('weight OF …'), in which a following noun is read in the genitive.
5.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — weight, heaviness; that which weighs in a balance

6.meaning: A single grain or seed, such as a kernel of grain; one small seed-unit of a plant.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun with the -in (tanwīn kasr) ending, marking the genitive case. The noun ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows it, so the form reads 'ḥabbatin'. The genitive is the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by another ('… of a grain'); the indefiniteness gives 'a grain'.
6.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — grain, seed; also love, affection

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: Mustard — the mustard plant, proverbially cited for its tiny seed as a byword for something extremely small.
8.grammar: A noun (collective, naming the plant). The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, the form a noun takes when indefinite and following a preposition or another noun (e.g. 'a grain of mustard'). It is famed for the minuteness of its seed.

9.meaning: then it be / it would be
9.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form I (كَانَ), 3rd person feminine singular; used in conditional apodosis

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: a rock
11.grammar: noun, feminine singular, genitive case with tanwīn (indefinite), object of preposition فِي (in) in the conditional clause

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

18.meaning: He/it comes, or brings. From the verb 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense of bringing or producing something.
18.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine. This root ends weakly in a vowel, and the bare form yati (without a final -ī) shows the jussive or apocopated mood, the clipped form used after conditional particles and in answers to conditions.

19.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
19.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
21.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: Means "subtle, gentle, finely perceptive" — an intensive descriptive term for one who is kind and gracious, whose awareness penetrates the most delicate and hidden things, acting with imperceptible tenderness.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ("a/one who is") and typically signals the word is functioning as a subject or predicate.

24.meaning: 'Fully aware / All-Aware' — one who knows the inner reality and hidden details of things through intimate, expert knowledge. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect awareness of all that is concealed.
24.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, thorough quality ('thoroughly aware'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamm): it marks an indefinite noun/adjective in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

1.meaning: An affectionate vocative meaning 'O my little son / O my dear son' — a tender, diminutive form of address from a parent to a son, with 'my' attached.
1.grammar: A vocative with the particle 'yā' for addressing someone. The base is an affectionate diminutive of 'son'. The attached possessive is the first-person -ī ('my'); because the diminutive stem already ends in a doubled yāʾ, the possessive -ī merges with it and the word is pronounced 'bunayya'. The whole is a loving 'O my dear son'.
1.root: ب-ن-ي / ب-ن-و (b-n-y) — son, offspring, to build

2.meaning: Establish! Set up firmly, perform fully and uprightly — a command to carry something out properly and keep it standing. Of prayer it means to observe it duly with all its conditions.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person ('you', masculine singular). Its base form ends in a silent stop; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster, not a case ending.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand; (causative) to set up, establish, perform

3.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
3.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

4.meaning: 'And command / and enjoin.' Combines 'and' with the singular imperative 'order' — to instruct or bid someone to do something.
4.grammar: wa- = 'and.' The rest is a singular imperative 'command/order' (you, one person). The form comes from a root whose initial hamza is normally elided, leaving 'mur'; the ending has no vowel (jussive/command form).

5.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

5.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
5.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

6.meaning: and forbid / prevent
6.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form I (نَهَى), 2nd person masculine singular; ا is prosthetic hamzah for ease of pronunciation

7.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

8.meaning: That which is rejected, disapproved, and recognized as wrong — what sound nature and revelation deem objectionable; 'the wrong' or 'the reprehensible'.
8.grammar: A noun (originally a passive participle, 'that which is denied/rejected') with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

9.meaning: And be patient / endure steadfastly / persevere — sabr is the disciplined restraint of the self: bearing hardship calmly, holding firm, and not giving way to impatience or despair. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'be patient!', carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is the normal shape of the singular command form.
9.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself, persevere

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: Verb meaning 'it struck / befell / reached (you)' — that some event landed upon and touched a person. The verb is neutral in itself and applies equally to good fortune and to harm or hardship.
12.grammar: A past-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he'). The unchanging '-a' on 'aṣāba' is the standard past-tense vowel. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular), giving 'it befell you.'
12.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, strike correctly; to befall or reach

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
14.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: Firm resolve, determination, or settled purpose — the firmness of will to carry something through. In a possessive (genitive) form, it conveys 'firm resolve of …' or 'the firm purpose of …'
16.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or comes after a preposition. It signals that this noun is possessed by, or stands in relation to, whatever follows it.
16.root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m) — to resolve firmly, to be determined

17.meaning: The matters, the affairs, the commands — the plural of 'amr,' covering things that are dealt with, ordered, or that come to pass. The definite article makes it 'the matters/affairs.'
17.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). Its own opening hamza is a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) that drops in pronunciation after the 'al-', so the cluster is read smoothly as 'al-umūr' even though the underlying noun is أُمُور. The final -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a possessing noun ('… of THE matters') or coming after a preposition.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: turn (your cheek) / twist

parts.en: do not turn away (jussive, Form II)

2.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form II (صَعَّرَ), 2nd person masculine singular, used after negative lā; meaning to turn aside in pride/contempt
2.root: ص-ع-ر (ṣ-ʿ-r) — to turn aside, to have neck disease causing crookedness

3.meaning: your cheek
3.grammar: noun, masculine singular, accusative case (direct object of تُصَعِّرْ) in construct with 2nd person singular possessive suffix كَ

4.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: You walk, go on foot, or proceed; to move along by walking. A verb of walking or going about.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks the subject as second-person ('you', masculine singular). The stem ends without a final vowel (the weak final letter dropped), the jussive mood, which typically follows a prohibition or negation ('do not …').
6.root: م-ش-ي (m-sh-y) — to walk, to go on foot

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: With exultant arrogance, insolent self-importance, or boastful glee; a swaggering, conceited manner of conduct. maraḥ denotes excessive, haughty elation.
9.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) frequently marks the manner or circumstance in which an action is done ('… in a state of arrogance'), describing how one behaves.
9.root: م-ر-ح (m-r-ḥ) — to be boisterously elated, exultant, or insolent

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
13.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

14.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
14.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

15.meaning: self-conceited / arrogant
15.grammar: active participle, Form VIII (اخْتَالَ), masculine singular, genitive case with tanwīn, functioning as adjective/ḥāl
15.root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l) — to imagine, to strut with pride; horse

16.grammar: intensive adjective (فَعُول pattern), masculine singular, genitive case with tanwīn, functioning as second adjective describing the arrogant person
16.root: ف-خ-ر (f-kh-r) — to boast, to be proud, to glory

1.meaning: and be moderate in
1.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form I (قَصَدَ), 2nd person masculine singular; ا is prosthetic hamzah; meaning to be moderate, to aim, to walk steadily
1.root: ق-ص-د (q-ṣ-d) — to aim for, to be moderate, to intend

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: your pace / your gait
3.grammar: noun, masculine singular, genitive case (object of verb اقْصِدْ in its nominal sense) in construct with 2nd person possessive suffix كَ; verbal noun (مصدر) of مَشَى

4.meaning: and lower
4.grammar: verb, imperative mood, Form I (غَضَّ), 2nd person masculine singular; ا is prosthetic hamzah; meaning to lower, to restrain, to reduce
4.root: غ-ض-ض (gh-ḍ-ḍ) — to lower, to restrain, to reduce

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: your voice
6.grammar: noun, masculine singular, genitive case (object of verb اغْضُضْ in construct) with 2nd person possessive suffix كَ

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: harshest / most repugnant
8.grammar: elative adjective (أَفْعَل pattern used for superlative), masculine singular, accusative case, meaning 'most repugnant / harshest'
8.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to deny, to reject; to be unknown, repugnant

9.meaning: of (all) voices / sounds
9.grammar: noun, broken plural of صَوْت, genitive case (object of preposition or in partitive construction with أَنكَر), definite with article

10.meaning: surely the voice / sound
10.grammar: emphatic particle لَ (lām al-ibtidāʾ) + noun صَوْت in nominative construct state, subject of the emphasis

11.meaning: of the donkeys
11.grammar: noun, broken plural of حِمَار (donkey), genitive case (in iḍāfa with preceding صَوْت), definite with article

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: you see / look
2.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form I (رَأَى), 2nd person masculine plural (final waw retained in jussive after dropping the weak letter ا in singular pattern)
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, to look

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: To make subservient, to harness or press into service; to bring something under control so it obediently serves a purpose. The Form II verb intensifies the sense of subjugating for use.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form II (to make serve). The bare form with final -a marks a completed action by a single masculine 'he' ('he made subservient').
5.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, harness, press into service

6.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
9.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

13.meaning: and amply bestowed / lavished

parts.en: He lavished / amply bestowed (past tense, Form IV)

13.grammar: verb, perfect tense, Form IV (أَسْبَغَ), 3rd person masculine singular, meaning to bestow abundantly, to complete fully
13.root: س-ب-غ (s-b-gh) — to be ample, to lavish, to complete

14.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
14.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

15.meaning: His bounties / blessings

parts.en: His (3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix)

15.grammar: noun, broken plural of نِعْمَة (blessing), accusative case (direct object of أَسْبَغَ) in construct with 3rd person masculine possessive suffix هُ
15.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — blessing, bounty; to be comfortable

16.grammar: active participle, Form I, feminine singular, accusative case with tanwīn; functioning as adjective modifying نِعَم (blessings)
16.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, to become manifest

17.grammar: active participle, Form I, feminine singular, accusative case with tanwīn; functioning as second adjective modifying نِعَم (blessings)
17.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — to be hidden, inner; belly

18.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
18.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

19.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
19.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
19.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

20.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
20.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

21.meaning: He argues, disputes, or pleads — contending back and forth in debate. The Form III pattern carries the sense of a reciprocal dispute between parties.
21.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he …'), shown by the yu- prefix. The final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a simple statement of fact. The Form III pattern signals a mutual, back-and-forth action.

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
24.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
24.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

25.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
25.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

26.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
26.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

27.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

27.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

28.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
28.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

29.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
29.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
29.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

30.grammar: active participle, Form IV (أَنَارَ), masculine singular, genitive case with tanwīn; functioning as adjective or predicate
30.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, to illuminate; light

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

3.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

4.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'follow!' / 'go after and conform to.' The verb means to walk behind someone, to imitate, obey, or adopt as one's way — to make oneself a follower of a path, person, or teaching.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) of a Form VIII verb, addressed to more than one person. The -ū ending marks a plural masculine command, 'you all [do it]!' The doubled-t stem (itta-) gives the reflexive/intensive sense of taking something on for oneself, i.e. making oneself a follower.

5.meaning: what / that which
5.grammar: relative pronoun (اسم موصول), indeclinable, used here as object of a preposition or as a relative pronoun meaning 'what'

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
6.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

9.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

10.meaning: 'We follow / we are following.' To go after, conform to, obey, or imitate — to take something as the way one walks behind and adheres to.
10.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The na- prefix means 'we [do/are doing]'; the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a subjunctive). The doubled-t stem gives the sense of taking something on as one's own way.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
12.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

13.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
13.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

14.meaning: 'Our fathers / forefathers / ancestors.' The plural of 'father,' denoting forebears and the line of those who came before, with the attached 'our' marking them as one's own ancestry.
14.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used to mark the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or certain adverbial roles.

15.meaning: A clustered opener used to challenge or press a point: roughly 'even if…?' / 'what, even though…?' It joins a questioning hamza ('really?'), the connector 'wa' (and), and 'law' (if/though), introducing a hypothetical that is being questioned or objected to.
15.grammar: A combination of particles: the question-marker a- (turning the phrase into a rhetorical challenge), the conjunction wa- ('and/even'), and the conditional law ('if/though'), which introduces a hypothetical condition. Being particles, none of them take case endings.

16.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

16.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

17.meaning: Shayṭān / Satan — a rebellious, malevolent being who incites to evil; the term denotes one that is remote from goodness and given to misleading. With 'al-', it points to the well-known devil.
17.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'sh', doubling it). 'shayṭān' is a noun for a devil or inciter of evil. The final -u is nominative, the form a word takes as the subject or doer of an action.

parts.en: them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

18.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form I (دَعَا), 3rd person masculine singular, indicative; with 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun هُمْ
18.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to supplicate

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
19.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

20.meaning: ʿAdhāb — punishment, torment, suffering inflicted as a penalty; severe chastisement.
20.grammar: A noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word names painful punishment and torment.

21.meaning: The Blaze — a fiercely kindled, flaming fire. On its pattern the word stresses an intensely blazing, raging fire, and it is used as a name for the punishing Fire.
21.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'; its 'l' assimilates into the following 's' in pronunciation (heard as-saʿīr). The word is on the faʿīl pattern, here conveying an intense, kindled fire. The final -i is the genitive ending, used after a preposition or in possessive linkage ('… OF …').
21.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, blaze, flare up

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: submits / surrenders
2.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form IV (أَسْلَمَ), 3rd person masculine singular; used in conditional clause
2.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — to be safe, to submit, to surrender

3.meaning: His face; the front of the head — and by extension one's whole self, presence, or the direction in which one turns. 'Surrendering one's face' idiomatically means devoting one's entire being.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu meaning 'his.' The -a on the stem is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). With the pronoun it means 'his face/self.'
3.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, aspect; what one turns toward

4.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
4.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
6.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

7.meaning: One who does good; a person of excellence who acts beautifully and rightly — doing good to others and performing deeds with sincerity and mastery, as though aware of being watched by Allah (iḥsān).

parts.en: doer of good / one of excellence

7.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) meaning 'one who does good,' formed from the four-letter (causative) pattern. The ending -un is the nominative case with 'nunation' (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun), the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or what something is equated with — here 'a good-doer.'
7.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — beauty, goodness, excellence; to do well/beautifully

8.meaning: 'Then/so, indeed …' — the connector 'then/so' joined to the particle 'qad', which before a past-tense verb stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
8.grammar: A connecting particle 'fa-' ('then/so', often signalling a result) plus 'qad'. With a following perfect verb, 'qad' emphasises that the act is real and completed ('have indeed …'). The final -i on 'qad' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster; it carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

9.meaning: He took firm hold; he gripped and clung tightly, holding fast and refusing to let go.
9.grammar: A Form X past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he held fast"). The ista- pattern often adds an intensive or sought-after sense — here, a deliberate, firm seizing. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a single masculine subject.
9.root: م-س-ك (m-s-k) — to hold, grasp, retain, grip

10.meaning: By/with the handhold — the firm grip, the secure handle or loop that one seizes to keep from falling.
10.grammar: The prefix bi- ("by/with") governs the following noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending. The al- prefix makes the noun definite ("the"). It is a feminine singular noun.
10.root: ع-ر-و (ʿ-r-w) — to cling to, a handhold, a loop or bond one grasps

11.meaning: the most trustworthy handhold

parts.en: the most trustworthy / firmest (definite, superlative feminine)

11.grammar: elative adjective in feminine form (فُعْلَى pattern = superlative), definite with article, nominative/genitive; describes الْعُرْوَة (the handhold)
11.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to be firm, reliable, trustworthy

12.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
14.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
14.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

15.meaning: The matters, the affairs, the commands — the plural of 'amr,' covering things that are dealt with, ordered, or that come to pass. The definite article makes it 'the matters/affairs.'
15.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). Its own opening hamza is a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) that drops in pronunciation after the 'al-', so the cluster is read smoothly as 'al-umūr' even though the underlying noun is أُمُور. The final -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a possessing noun ('… of THE matters') or coming after a preposition.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
3.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'it grieves you' or 'it makes you sad' — to cause sorrow, distress, or anxiety to a single addressee.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') marked by the 'ya-' prefix. The vowel-less (jussive) ending on the stem shows it follows a governing particle such as a negative or conditional. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male).

5.meaning: his disbelief / ungratefulness

parts.en: his (3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix)

5.grammar: noun, masculine singular, nominative case (subject of sentence) in construct with 3rd person masculine possessive suffix هُ
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, to be ungrateful, to cover

6.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
6.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

7.meaning: Their place or act of return — the destination to which a group comes back, their returning or homecoming.
7.grammar: A noun of place/occasion built on the ma- pattern ('the place or moment of returning'), with the attached pronoun -hum ('their,' a male/mixed group) showing possession. The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, typically marking the subject or the thing being identified ('their return [is …]').

8.meaning: then We will inform them

parts.en: them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

8.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form II (نَبَّأَ), 1st person plural (majestic we), indicative; with 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun هُمْ
8.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — to inform, to give news

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
10.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
10.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

14.meaning: "Of what is within / the contents of" — literally 'with that which possesses', an idiom for the innermost contents or true nature of something. The feminine word dhāt means 'possessor of' and so 'that which holds/contains'.
14.grammar: The feminine noun 'dhāt' ('possessor/owner of') governed by the preposition 'bi-', hence the genitive -i ending used after prepositions. 'Dhāt' is grammatically a construct word: it expects a following noun, giving the sense 'that which holds/contains …'.
14.root: — (function word built on the idea of 'possessor of')

15.meaning: "The breasts / chests" — the chests of human beings, commonly used as the seat of the heart, feelings, intentions, and innermost thoughts.
15.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the chests'). The -i ending is the genitive case, typically linking it to a preceding word ('… OF …') or following a preposition. 'Ṣudūr' is the plural of 'ṣadr' (chest/breast).
15.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, breast, the foremost part

1.meaning: We grant them enjoyment

parts.en: We grant enjoyment to (imperfect, Form II)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

1.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form II (مَتَّعَ), 1st person plural (majestic we), indicative; with 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun هُمْ
1.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to benefit, to grant enjoyment

2.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
2.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
2.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

3.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
3.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

4.meaning: We will drive them / force them

parts.en: We will compel / drive (imperfect, Form VIII)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

4.grammar: verb, imperfect tense, Form VIII (اضْطَرَّ), 1st person plural (majestic we), indicative; with 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun هُمْ; meaning to compel, to force
4.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm; to compel, to be forced

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
6.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'harsh, rough, severe, coarse' — thick or crude in texture, and by extension stern, grievous, or heavy when describing punishment or treatment.
7.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite; this ending typically appears when the word follows a preposition or modifies a genitive (often-translated '… of …') noun.
7.root: غ-ل-ظ (gh-l-ẓ) — to be thick, coarse, harsh, severe

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'
2.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, request

3.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

4.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
4.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

6.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
6.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

7.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
7.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

10.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
10.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.

11.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
11.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

12.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

13.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
13.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
13.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
15.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence; a counted noun normally follows it in the genitive plural ('seven of ...').

14.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
